question.text: Let $\langle x,y,z \rangle$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. \[ \begin{cases} 3x + 2y + z = 1 \\ 5x + 3y + 4z = 2 \\ x + y - z = 1 \end{cases} \] Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-1,$ then $x=$
question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

\[ \begin{cases} {\color{blue}3}x + {\color{blue}2}y + {\color{blue}1}z = {\color{red}1} \\ {\color{blue}5}x + {\color{blue}3}y+ {\color{blue}4}z = {\color{red}2} \\ {\color{blue}1}x + {\color{blue}1}y + ({\color{blue}-1})z = {\color{red}1}. \end{cases} \]

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

\begin{align} D = \left|\begin{matrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}1 \\ \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}4 \\ \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-1 \end{matrix}\right| = -1. \end{align}

Now, to find $D_x$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

\begin{align} D_x = \left|\begin{matrix} \color{red}1 & \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}1 \\ \color{red}2 & \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}4 \\ \color{red}1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-1 \end{matrix}\right| &= 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} - 2 \cdot\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} + 1 \cdot\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] & = (-3 - 4) - 2(-2 - 4) + (2 - 3) \\[5pt] & = -7 + 12 - 1 \\[5pt] & = 4. \end{align}

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

\begin{align} x & = \dfrac {D_x} D = \dfrac {4} {-1} = -4. \end{align}

question.text:
Let $\langle x,y,z \rangle$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. \[ \begin{cases} 2x - y + 2z = 6 \\ 3x + 2y - z = k \\ 4x + 3y - 3z = 1 \end{cases} \]

Given that $x=1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-9,$ find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

\begin{align} D = \left|\begin{matrix} 2 & -1 & 2\\ 3 & 2 & -1\\ 4 & 3 & -3 \end{matrix}\right| = -9 \end{align}

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x = \dfrac{D_x}{D},$ where

\begin{align} D_x = \left|\begin{matrix} 6 & -1 & 2\\ k & 2 & -1\\ 1 & 3 & -3 \end{matrix}\right| & = 6 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 \end{matrix}\right| - (-1) \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & -3 \end{matrix}\right| + 2 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} k & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{matrix}\right|\\[5pt] & = 6(-6 +3) + (-3k + 1) + 2(3k - 2) \\[5pt] & = -18 -3k + 1 +6k - 4 \\[5pt] & = 3k - 21. \end{align}

Therefore, we have

\[ x = \dfrac{D_x}{D} = \dfrac{3k-21}{-9}. \]

From the problem statement, we know that $x=1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

\begin{align} \dfrac {-9}{3k-21} & = 1 \\[5pt] -9 & = 3k - 21 \\[5pt] 12 & = 3k \\[5pt] k & = 4. \end{align}

question.text:
Let $\langle x,y,z \rangle$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below.

\[ \begin{cases} 3x - 3y = 1 \\ 5x + 4y - 2z = 0 \\ y - z = 3 \end{cases} \]

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-21,$ then $y=$
question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

\[ \begin{cases} {\color{blue}3}x + ({\color{blue}-3})y + {\color{blue}0}z = {\color{red}1} \\ {\color{blue}5}x + {\color{blue}4}y + ({\color{blue}-2})z = {\color{red}0} \\ {\color{blue}0}x + {\color{blue}1}y + ({\color{blue}-1}) z = {\color{red}3} \end{cases} \]

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

\begin{align} D = \left|\begin{matrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-3 & \color{blue}0\\ \color{blue}5 & \color{blue}4 & \color{blue}-2\\ \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-1 \end{matrix}\right| = -21 \end{align}

Now, to find $D_y,$ we take the coefficients matrix, replace the second column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

\begin{align} D_y = \left|\begin{matrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{red}1 & \color{blue}0\\ \color{blue}5 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}-2\\ \color{blue}0 & \color{red}3 & \color{blue}-1 \end{matrix}\right| & = 3 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 \end{matrix}\right| -1 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \end{matrix}\right| + 0 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 \end{matrix}\right|\\[5pt] & = 3(0 + 6) - (-5 - 0) + 0 \\[5pt] & = 18 + 5 \\[5pt] & = 23. \end{align}

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

\begin{align} y & = \dfrac {D_y} D = \dfrac {23}{-21} = -\dfrac{23}{21}. \end{align}

question.text:
Let $\langle x,y,z \rangle$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. \[ \begin{cases} 3x - 5y - 2z = -7 \\ 2x +y - 4 z = -10 \\ 3x -3y -2 z = -7 \end{cases} \]

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $16,$ then $z=$
question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

\[ \begin{cases} {\color{blue}3}x + ({\color{blue}-5})y + ({\color{blue}-2}z) = {\color{red}-7} \\ {\color{blue}2}x + {\color{blue}1}y+ ({\color{blue}-4})z = {\color{red}-10} \\ {\color{blue}3}x + ({\color{blue}-3})y + ({\color{blue}-2})z = {\color{red}-7}. \end{cases} \]

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

\begin{align} D = \left|\begin{matrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-5 & \color{blue}-2\\ \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-4\\ \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-3 & \color{blue}-2 \end{matrix}\right| = 16. \end{align}

Now, to find $D_z$, we replace the third column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

\begin{align} D_z = \left|\begin{matrix} \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-5 & \color{blue}-7\\ \color{blue}2 & \color{blue}1 & \color{blue}-10\\ \color{blue}3 & \color{blue}-3 & \color{blue}-7 \end{matrix}\right| & = 3 \cdot\left|\begin{matrix} 1 & -10 \\ -3 & -7 \end{matrix}\right| - (-5) \cdot\left|\begin{matrix} 2 & -10 \\ 3 & -7 \end{matrix}\right| +(- 7) \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -3 \end{matrix}\right|\\[5pt] & = 3(-7-30) + 5(-14+30) -7(-6-3)\\[5pt] & = -111 + 80 + 63\\[5pt] & = 32. \end{align}

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

\begin{align} z & = \dfrac {D_z} D = \dfrac {32} {16} = 2. \end{align}

question.text:
Let $\langle x,y,z \rangle$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. \[ \begin{cases} 3x - 4y - 5z = 1 \\ 2x + 3y - 3z = k \\ -5x + 3y + 7z = -2 \end{cases} \]

Given that $y=-1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-19,$ find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

\begin{align} D = \left|\begin{matrix} 3 & -4 & -5\\ 2 & 3 & -3\\ -5 & 3 & 7 \end{matrix}\right| = -19 \end{align}

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y = \dfrac{D_y}{D},$ where

\begin{align} D_y = \left|\begin{matrix} 3 & 1 & -5\\ 2 & k & -3\\ -5 & -2 & 7 \end{matrix}\right| & = 3 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} k & -3 \\ -2 & 7 \end{matrix}\right| - 1 \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 7 \end{matrix}\right| + (-5) \cdot \left|\begin{matrix} 2 & k \\ -5 & -2 \end{matrix}\right|\\[5pt] & = 3(7k - 6) - (14-15) - 5(-4+5k) \\[5pt] & = 21k - 18 + 1 + 20 - 25k \\[5pt] & = -4k + 3. \end{align}

Therefore, we have

\[ y = \dfrac{D_y}{D} = \dfrac{-4k+3}{-19}. \]

From the problem statement, we know that $y=-1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

\begin{align} \dfrac{-4k+3}{-19} & = -1 \\[5pt] -4k+3 & = 19\\[5pt] -4k & = 16\\[5pt] k & = -4. \end{align}
